title: SELECT

options.a: The projection clause specifying the target list of output expressions, aliases, and functions to return.
options.b: The execution clause responsible for materializing intermediate relation sets into temporary work_mem buffers.
options.c: The query directive that defines physical heap scan strategies and binds relation descriptors into range tables.
options.d: The command that evaluates boolean predicates across candidate tuples and eliminates non-matching rows before return.

postanswer: SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users;

title: FROM

options.a: Specifies physical block offsets and heap file paths to initiate low-level POSIX file read operations.
options.b: Specifies source table references, subqueries, joins, or functions that populate query range tables.
options.c: The clause that binds output projection columns directly to shared buffer pages and enforces table locks.
options.d: Declares the temporary tablespace allocation and work_mem memory quotas for intermediate join processing.

postanswer: SELECT u.username, p.title FROM users u JOIN posts p ON u.id = p.user_id;

title: WHERE

options.a: A post-projection filter evaluated after LIMIT and OFFSET have constrained candidate rows in the plan.
options.b: Filters output groups and aggregate results after GROUP BY execution by evaluating a group condition.
options.c: Filters rows emitted by FROM by evaluating a boolean expression on each candidate tuple prior to grouping.
options.d: A conditional clause evaluated strictly after window functions to eliminate rows from client projection lists.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount > 250.00;

title: GROUP BY

options.a: Reorganizes physical table storage on disk into clustered bucket pages matching unique column hash keys.
options.b: Sorts the result set in heap memory and removes duplicate adjacent rows without computing aggregates in engine.
options.c: Partitions incoming row streams into distinct window frames while preserving individual input rows for math.
options.d: Condenses selected rows sharing identical grouping values into summary rows, establishing aggregate context.

postanswer: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) AS total_staff, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: HAVING

options.a: Filters grouped rows or aggregate results by evaluating a boolean condition strictly after GROUP BY runs.
options.b: Pre-filters individual candidate tuples from relation scans before grouping to avoid aggregating raw rows.
options.c: Imposes a check constraint condition on newly inserted or updated rows within a data manipulation statement.
options.d: Filters rows generated across window frames after analytic window function calculations have produced values.

postanswer: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 75000;

title: ORDER BY

options.a: Forces the query planner to choose an index scan over a sequential scan by declaring physical read order.
options.b: Sorts output tuples based on specified expressions, collation rules, and direction (ASC/DESC/NULLS) options.
options.c: Partitions and sorts candidate rows strictly within the local boundaries of an analytic window frame in SQL.
options.d: Reorders physical storage blocks on disk to permanently match B-tree index key order during statement execution.

postanswer: SELECT id, name, created_at FROM customers ORDER BY created_at DESC NULLS LAST;

title: LIMIT

options.a: Restricts maximum memory allocated to work_mem for sorting and hash operations within the query plan tree.
options.b: Sets the execution timeout in milliseconds for the query before the executor raises an execution abort error.
options.c: Constrains the maximum number of rows returned by the query executor to a non-negative integer count or expression.
options.d: Limits the maximum number of shared buffer pages the query executor is allowed to read during sequential scans.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM audit_logs ORDER BY log_time DESC LIMIT 10;

title: OFFSET

options.a: Adjusts column positions and indices within composite or array data types when projecting structured attributes.
options.b: Specifies a physical byte offset from the start of the PostgreSQL heap file to begin reading tuple headers directly.
options.c: Delays query execution by a specified number of milliseconds to throttle client request frequencies in background.
options.d: Skips a specified number of rows from the beginning of the result set before returning rows to the caller client.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40;

title: FETCH FIRST

options.a: SQL-standard syntax equivalent to LIMIT specifying the maximum row count (or percentage with WITH TIES) to return.
options.b: Cursor retrieval directive pulling only the first tuple from a declared portal into client memory and closing it.
options.c: An optimization hint instructing the planner to choose an execution plan minimizing startup cost rather than total.
options.d: Executor directive returning the first row encountered in physical storage without waiting for ORDER BY sorting.

postanswer: SELECT id, title, score FROM movies ORDER BY score DESC FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY;

title: FETCH NEXT

options.a: A procedural PL/pgSQL keyword used inside loops to fetch the subsequent record from an implicit refcursor.
options.b: SQL-standard syntax alternative to FETCH FIRST used to constrain returned rows, semantically equivalent to LIMIT.
options.c: A cursor navigation command advancing an open cursor to the next tuple relative to current portal position in query.
options.d: A replication primitive instructing standby servers to fetch the next sequential WAL record from primary database.

postanswer: SELECT id, rank FROM players ORDER BY rank ASC OFFSET 10 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS WITH TIES;

title: FOR UPDATE

options.a: Acquires a Share lock on selected rows that allows concurrent reads but defers all incoming writes until commit time.
options.b: An immediate DML directive that updates column values in place during a SELECT scan without generating WAL records log.
options.c: Acquires Exclusive row locks on selected rows, blocking concurrent updates, deletes, or locks until transaction commit.
options.d: Acquires a weaker lock than FOR NO KEY UPDATE permitting concurrent transactions to acquire FOR KEY SHARE locks.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM bank_accounts WHERE account_id = 42 FOR UPDATE;

title: FOR NO KEY UPDATE

options.a: Locks rows exclusively without writing tuple transaction IDs (XMAX) into heap page headers, avoiding bloat.
options.b: Acquires an exclusive row-level lock that explicitly prevents foreign key constraints from evaluating during commit.
options.c: A read-only locking clause preventing concurrent transactions from dropping indexes referenced by the current query.
options.d: Acquires a weaker row lock than FOR UPDATE that blocks updates/deletes but permits concurrent FOR KEY SHARE locks.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = 101 FOR NO KEY UPDATE;

title: FOR SHARE

options.a: Acquires a Shared row lock preventing updates or deletes on selected rows while allowing concurrent reads and shares.
options.b: Acquires an exclusive table-level ShareLock preventing concurrent schema alterations while permitting inserts.
options.c: Shares cached query plans and execution state across multiple backend worker processes in a parallel query worker group.
options.d: Temporarily marks selected rows read-only across the database cluster, persisting beyond transaction completion on disk.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM flight_seats WHERE flight_id = 'AA100' FOR SHARE;

title: FOR KEY SHARE

options.a: Acquires an exclusive lock on all B-tree index pages referencing the selected primary key or unique key values.
options.b: Acquires the weakest row lock, blocking only FOR UPDATE while permitting concurrent readers and key share locks.
options.c: Locks cryptographic encryption keys associated with transparent column encryption for the duration of the query.
options.d: Prevents concurrent transactions from inserting new rows that match key distribution of currently selected rows.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM parent_categories WHERE id = 5 FOR KEY SHARE;

title: NOWAIT

options.a: Causes the transaction to commit asynchronously without waiting for write-ahead log (WAL) flushes to disk storage.
options.b: Bypasses the lock manager completely and performs dirty reads on tuples currently locked by uncommitted transactions.
options.c: Modifies row-locking clauses to immediately raise an error if any selected row cannot be locked without waiting.
options.d: Skips rows that cannot be locked immediately and continues returning only unencumbered matching rows to client.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM inventory_items WHERE sku = 'ITEM-999' FOR UPDATE NOWAIT;

title: SKIP LOCKED

options.a: Aborts query execution immediately if any candidate row is found to be locked by an active concurrent transaction.
options.b: Releases acquired row locks immediately after reading each tuple, before the transaction execution completes.
options.c: Bypasses relation-level AccessExclusive locks to read table data directly while an ALTER TABLE operation is pending.
options.d: Modifies row-locking clauses to skip rows currently locked by other transactions, returning only free rows.

postanswer: SELECT id, payload FROM task_queue WHERE status = 'pending' LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;

title: INSERT

options.a: Appends new tuples into a target table, evaluating default expressions, check constraints, and firing INSERT triggers.
options.b: Overwrites existing records in a relation with new column values, creating an updated MVCC tuple version in table heap.
options.c: Modifies relation schemas by adding new data structures or column definitions to internal system catalogs.
options.d: Bulk-loads unparsed text streams directly from the operating system into heap pages without transactional overhead in engine.

postanswer: INSERT INTO customers (name, email) VALUES ('Alice Johnson', 'alice@example.com');

title: INTO

options.a: An isolation modifier that forces inserted tuples to be routed into temporary tablespaces rather than main storage.
options.b: Specifies target tables in INSERT statements or output variables/tables in PL/pgSQL and legacy SELECT queries.
options.c: A clause that specifies the source relation from which data streams are extracted for ingestion into storage.
options.d: Directs query output to be serialized into a client-side JSON format instead of standard tabular wire protocol.

postanswer: INSERT INTO archive_orders SELECT * FROM active_orders WHERE status = 'archived';

title: UPDATE

options.a: Modifies table schema definitions in pg_attribute without altering existing tuple binary storage in heap pages.
options.b: Overwrites heap tuple bytes in place on disk without incrementing transaction visibility identifiers or writing WAL.
options.c: Modifies existing rows by writing new MVCC tuple versions with updated values while marking old versions expired.
options.d: Refreshes cached materialization data for materialized views without re-executing underlying defining queries.

postanswer: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 50.00, updated_at = NOW() WHERE account_id = 12;

title: SET

options.a: Declares a collection of unique distinct values within a WHERE clause equivalent to an expanded array literal.
options.b: Converts a scalar subquery into a table-valued set relation for set-theoretic union and intersection operations.
options.c: Binds an execution plan to a specific prepared statement handle in server session memory for subsequent executions.
options.d: Specifies column-value assignments in UPDATE statements or configures runtime parameters in session commands.

postanswer: UPDATE users SET is_active = TRUE, status = 'verified' WHERE verification_token = 'xyz123';

title: DELETE

options.a: Removes rows from a table by marking tuple versions as dead (setting XMAX) without immediate physical disk deallocation.
options.b: Truncates table storage blocks instantly by reinitializing relation file forks without recording undo logging.
options.c: Drops column constraints and removes foreign key references from system catalog tables across all active schemas in cluster.
options.d: Reverts uncommitted transaction changes and restores modified tuples to their initial state prior to statement execution.

postanswer: DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires_at < NOW();

title: VALUES

options.a: Extracts current runtime values of PostgreSQL GUC configuration variables from shared server memory tables.
options.b: Constructs a constant table expression from row expressions, usable in INSERT statements or as standalone queries.
options.c: A schema declaration clause that specifies default column values inside a CREATE TABLE definition for new tuples.
options.d: Formats raw query output into human-readable tabular text strings within the psql command-line interface terminal.

postanswer: INSERT INTO status_codes (code, label) VALUES (200, 'OK'), (404, 'Not Found'), (500, 'Server Error');

title: COPY

options.a: Duplicates an entire table schema and data into a new table within the same schema using logical replication streams.
options.b: Performs a physical block-level clone of relation data fork files across different tablespaces without locking.
options.c: Streams data between PostgreSQL tables and file systems or STDIN/STDOUT, bypassing normal SQL parsing overhead.
options.d: Creates a snapshot backup of WAL logs and dirty buffer pages to external archive storage for point-in-time recovery.

postanswer: COPY transactions FROM '/var/data/transactions_2026.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true);

title: RETURNING

options.a: Reverts modified rows back to their pre-transaction states if an unhandled exception occurs in a trigger function run.
options.b: Returns execution plan statistics and physical I/O costs of a DML operation instead of modified row counts.
options.c: Forces an asynchronous DML statement to return control immediately to client applications without waiting for disk WAL.
options.d: Projects and returns expressions or column values of rows modified by INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE directly to client.

postanswer: INSERT INTO users (username) VALUES ('jdoe') RETURNING id, created_at;

title: ON CONFLICT

options.a: Defines an upsert clause for INSERT statements, specifying a target and alternative action upon unique collision.
options.b: Resolves deadlock conditions automatically by choosing which transaction to abort based on priority weights.
options.c: Defines exception-handling logic inside PL/pgSQL blocks when a unique_violation error code is raised at runtime execution.
options.d: Detects concurrent serializable transaction conflicts and automatically retries the failed transaction block in server.

postanswer: INSERT INTO user_preferences (user_id, theme) VALUES (42, 'dark') ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO NOTHING;

title: DO NOTHING

options.a: An empty execution statement in PL/pgSQL that serves as a no-op placeholder inside conditional execution branches.
options.b: An ON CONFLICT action that suppresses unique or exclusion violation errors, silently skipping conflicting rows.
options.c: A trigger action that prevents a trigger function from executing without aborting the parent statement execution.
options.d: A transaction modifier that marks the current transaction block as read-only and ignores all write operations.

postanswer: INSERT INTO tags (name) VALUES ('postgresql') ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING;

title: DO UPDATE

options.a: Forces an UPDATE statement to bypass foreign key constraint validation during high-throughput batch writes to storage.
options.b: Automatically updates all secondary index entries for a table when an unindexed column value changes in a row.
options.c: An ON CONFLICT action converting colliding INSERTs into UPDATEs on existing rows using the EXCLUDED pseudo-relation.
options.d: An anonymous code block executor that runs inline procedural code without creating a persistent stored function in catalog.

postanswer: INSERT INTO metrics (metric_key, hit_count) VALUES ('api_hits', 1) ON CONFLICT (metric_key) DO UPDATE SET hit_count = metrics.hit_count + EXCLUDED.hit_count;

title: OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE

options.a: Bypasses PostgreSQL system catalog permissions to insert rows into protected internal metadata catalog tables.
options.b: Overrides system default collation and character encoding rules for string literals in the current statement execution run.
options.c: Suppresses internal system-generated audit logging and WAL writing for low-level disaster recovery operations.
options.d: Directs INSERT to accept user-provided values for GENERATED ALWAYS identity columns, overriding sequence generation.

postanswer: INSERT INTO orders (id, amount) OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES (501, 199.99);

title: OVERRIDING USER VALUE

options.a: Directs INSERT to ignore user-supplied values for GENERATED BY DEFAULT identity columns, forcing sequence values.
options.b: Resets user-defined session configuration parameters back to database-wide system default values in postgresql.conf.
options.c: Strips user-defined column default expressions and forces column values to be inserted as NULL during transactions.
options.d: Overrides current role permissions with superuser system identity for the duration of the current query execution.

postanswer: INSERT INTO invoices (id, client_id) OVERRIDING USER VALUE VALUES (999, 42);

title: CREATE

options.a: Modifies system configuration parameters in postgresql.conf to allocate shared memory for new database processes.
options.b: Instantiates a new database object (table, index, view, role) and registers its metadata in system catalogs.
options.c: Compiles raw SQL text into an executable binary plan and registers it permanently in shared server cache memory.
options.d: Initializes a physical database cluster on disk by running the bootstrap initdb sequence and creating template1.

postanswer: CREATE TABLE employees (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, full_name TEXT NOT NULL);

title: ALTER

options.a: Modifies structural definitions, attributes, constraints, or storage options of existing database objects in catalogs.
options.b: Forces the immediate reallocation and reorganization of physical heap pages on disk without modifying catalog metadata.
options.c: Converts table data between different character encodings on the fly during physical sequential read scans of heap.
options.d: Dynamically modifies runtime query execution plans without altering catalog schema definitions or table attributes.

postanswer: ALTER TABLE employees ADD COLUMN date_of_birth DATE NOT NULL;

title: DROP

options.a: Removes rows from a relation while preserving table structure, primary keys, indexes, and associated catalog metadata.
options.b: Marks relation buffers in shared_buffers as dirty and immediately flushes them to disk without transaction commits.
options.c: Permanently deletes existing database objects from system catalogs and marks physical storage files for deallocation.
options.d: Revokes all access permissions from a specified role while leaving the target database object intact and unchanged.

postanswer: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS deprecated_logs CASCADE;

title: TRUNCATE

options.a: Removes all tuples by executing a sequential table scan, setting XMAX as dead and firing row-level DELETE triggers.
options.b: Decreases allocated column width of variable-length character columns (VARCHAR) in existing tables without locks.
options.c: Flushes server write-ahead logs (WAL) and truncates inactive WAL segments to reclaim filesystem storage space on disk.
options.d: Quickly empties tables by allocating new storage forks, acquiring AccessExclusiveLock, and bypassing row triggers.

postanswer: TRUNCATE TABLE session_cache RESTART IDENTITY;

title: TABLE

options.a: DDL keyword defining a relational container with typed attributes, constraints, and heap storage (or query shorthand).
options.b: A memory-only hash structure used exclusively for temporary caching during multi-stage hash joins in query execution.
options.c: A catalog view in pg_catalog that displays statistics about disk block usage across relation forks and table spaces.
options.d: An abstract data structure defining client-server wire protocol packet frames for tabular data exchange over TCP sockets.

postanswer: CREATE TABLE products (sku VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY, price NUMERIC(10,2));

title: INDEX

options.a: An in-memory dictionary cache that translates relation names into internal 32-bit Object Identifiers (OIDs) fast.
options.b: Auxiliary storage structure (e.g. B-tree, Hash, GIN, BRIN) built on columns to accelerate lookups and enforce uniqueness.
options.c: A sequential transaction identifier log used by the storage manager to determine MVCC visibility snapshots in memory.
options.d: A partition boundary mapping table that routes incoming rows to physical partition child relations during insertions on table.

postanswer: CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);

title: VIEW

options.a: A pre-computed physical heap table that automatically refreshes contents whenever underlying tables change via WAL replay logs.
options.b: A server-side window buffer that captures query execution metrics and explains planner cost estimations to users.
options.c: A virtual relation defined by a stored query, expanded inline by the query rewriter without independent physical storage.
options.d: A specialized foreign data wrapper that allows cross-database querying across distinct PostgreSQL cluster instances.

postanswer: CREATE VIEW active_users AS SELECT id, username, email FROM users WHERE is_active = TRUE;

title: MATERIALIZED VIEW

options.a: A cached client-side result set that automatically purges its contents when the backend session terminates.
options.b: A table-like object that persists query output on disk and requires explicit REFRESH commands to synchronize.
options.c: A temporary in-memory heap table populated during query parsing to speed up complex recursive CTE queries in memory.
options.d: A physical replication replica that applies write-ahead log updates asynchronously to maintain sync state on node.

postanswer: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW monthly_sales_summary AS SELECT date_trunc('month', sale_date) AS sale_month, SUM(amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY 1;

title: SCHEMA

options.a: A logical namespace in a database containing tables, views, types, and functions isolated from other namespaces.
options.b: A global authentication realm that groups database users and maps them to operating system user accounts on disk.
options.c: A physical storage layout specification that allocates data blocks across distinct tablespace disk partitions.
options.d: A compiled catalog cache containing serialized query execution plans and index selectivity statistics tables.

postanswer: CREATE SCHEMA analytics AUTHORIZATION data_team;

title: DATABASE

options.a: A physical cluster storage directory initialized by the initdb command that hosts multiple active backend nodes.
options.b: A logical group of relation partition tables distributed across shared memory segments for parallel executions.
options.c: A discrete set of schemas and objects providing isolated security and catalog boundaries within a cluster.
options.d: A dedicated tablespace on the local filesystem reserved for storing unlogged temporary relation data blocks.

postanswer: CREATE DATABASE production_db WITH OWNER = admin_user ENCODING = 'UTF8';

title: ROLE

options.a: A transaction isolation profile that defines lock escalation thresholds for high-concurrency server workloads.
options.b: An identity entity representing a user or group, holding global and object-level catalog permissions.
options.c: A procedural rule that intercepts client network connections and enforces TLS cryptographic certificate keys.
options.d: An execution privilege profile assigned to background worker processes for scheduled autovacuum operations.

postanswer: CREATE ROLE app_reader WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'secure_pass123';

title: USER

options.a: A database identity created with LOGIN permission by default, capable of opening client database sessions.
options.b: A temporary guest identity automatically assigned to unauthenticated socket connections from local UNIX sockets.
options.c: A client-side connection pooler parameter that determines maximum active client connections per backend pool.
options.d: An internal operating system service account that owns the PostgreSQL data directory binaries and config files.

postanswer: CREATE USER analyst_jane WITH PASSWORD 'StrongPassword99!';

title: GROUP

options.a: A memory allocation zone in work_mem dedicated to sorting data for GROUP BY and window aggregation operations.
options.b: A cluster of streaming replication standby nodes managed as a single automated failover high-availability unit.
options.c: A clause that clusters related table partitions together into a shared physical tablespace on fast storage.
options.d: A legacy SQL alias for a ROLE created NOLOGIN, commonly used to bundle privileges and grant them to users.

postanswer: CREATE GROUP report_viewers WITH USER alice, bob;

title: FUNCTION

options.a: A routine running in the caller transaction that accepts parameters and returns scalar, composite, or row sets.
options.b: An autonomous procedural block that always executes in an independent background worker with its own transaction.
options.c: A compiled C module that can commit or roll back the calling client outer transaction at arbitrary points.
options.d: A server-side trigger handler that cannot accept user arguments and cannot return any value back to callers.

postanswer: CREATE FUNCTION calculate_tax(subtotal NUMERIC) RETURNS NUMERIC AS $$ BEGIN RETURN subtotal * 0.08; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

title: PROCEDURE

options.a: A routine invoked via SELECT statements that is restricted to strictly read-only transactional operations.
options.b: A stored routine invoked with CALL that can manage transactions internally using COMMIT and ROLLBACK commands.
options.c: A client-side script executed by psql that preprocesses meta-commands before sending queries to the server process.
options.d: A background maintenance task registered in pg_cron that runs automated cleanup jobs at scheduled intervals daily.

postanswer: CREATE PROCEDURE purge_old_data(cutoff_date DATE) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN DELETE FROM audit_logs WHERE log_date < cutoff_date; COMMIT; END; $$;

title: TRIGGER

options.a: An automated scheduler inside the PostgreSQL backend that initiates vacuum tasks when bloat reaches limits.
options.b: A hardware interrupt handler that initiates crash recovery when disk controllers report I/O write failures.
options.c: A database object bound to a table executing a function BEFORE, AFTER, or INSTEAD OF specific SQL events.
options.d: A transaction log monitor that notifies streaming replication standbys when a WAL buffer has flushed to disk.

postanswer: CREATE TRIGGER trg_update_timestamp BEFORE UPDATE ON users FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION update_modified_column();

title: SEQUENCE

options.a: An array data structure storing ordered lists of timestamp values for time-series forecasting queries in engine.
options.b: The logical order in which the query planner sequences join operations between relations in a plan tree.
options.c: A continuous stream of write-ahead log records identified by monotonically increasing Log Sequence Numbers in WAL.
options.d: A single-row relation generating monotonic numbers concurrency-safely, unaffected by transaction rollbacks.

postanswer: CREATE SEQUENCE order_id_seq START WITH 1000 INCREMENT BY 1;

title: TYPE

options.a: A schema object defining a data type (enum, composite, range, base) with storage and I/O conversion methods.
options.b: A metadata flag categorizing tables as either regular heaps, unlogged relations, or temporary tables on disk.
options.c: An execution classification that distinguishes parallel-safe functions from parallel-restricted functions.
options.d: A storage engine parameter specifying whether column data is stored uncompressed, compressed, or in TOAST storage.

postanswer: CREATE TYPE order_status AS ENUM ('pending', 'processing', 'shipped', 'cancelled');

title: DOMAIN

options.a: A network security boundary that restricts incoming client connections based on reverse DNS hostnames.
options.b: A user-defined type based on an underlying type, augmented with optional DEFAULT values and CHECK rules.
options.c: A cluster of related databases that share common collation definitions and global authentication passwords.
options.d: A range of permitted integer values defined on sequence objects to prevent 32-bit numeric overflow errors.

postanswer: CREATE DOMAIN us_postal_code AS TEXT CHECK (VALUE ~ '^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$');

title: EXTENSION

options.a: A physical disk file that extends relation heap storage when a table exceeds the default 1GB segment limit.
options.b: A client protocol add-on that enables bidirectional streaming of binary result sets across web sockets.
options.c: A package bundling SQL objects (functions, types, operators, index methods) installable as a unified unit.
options.d: A runtime configuration flag that enables experimental PostgreSQL query planner algorithms and cost models.

postanswer: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";

title: TABLESPACE

options.a: An internal memory pool within shared_buffers reserved for sorting operations when work_mem is exhausted in pool.
options.b: A disk directory location outside the main data directory where database tables and indexes can be stored.
options.c: The logical namespace within a database schema that groups related tables for permission administration tasks.
options.d: The total allocated virtual memory address space available to a PostgreSQL backend worker process handle.

postanswer: CREATE TABLESPACE fast_ssd LOCATION '/mnt/fast_nvme/pg_data';

title: COLLATION

options.a: A schema object defining character sorting and comparison rules (linguistic order, case) via ICU or OS.
options.b: The internal process of combining and deduplicating index pages during B-tree background vacuum routines.
options.c: A network protocol layer that compresses character data before transmission across client socket channels.
options.d: A hashing function used to distribute rows evenly across hash partitions in a partitioned database table.

postanswer: CREATE COLLATION french_ci (provider = icu, locale = 'fr-FR-u-ks-level1', deterministic = false);

title: POLICY

options.a: An automated backup retention schedule that defines how long WAL archive segments are preserved on disk volumes.
options.b: A load-balancing configuration profile that distributes read-only queries across standby read replicas.
options.c: An RLS rule defining conditions controlling which rows a specific role can select, insert, update, or delete.
options.d: A server resource limit that restricts maximum CPU core consumption and memory usage per database role.

postanswer: CREATE POLICY user_policy ON user_records FOR ALL TO app_user USING (user_id = current_setting('app.current_user_id')::INTEGER);

title: RULE

options.a: A database constraint that forces table column values to match an external regular expression check pattern.
options.b: A query rewrite mechanism that transforms incoming SQL query trees into alternate or additional query trees.
options.c: A connection authorization rule defined in pg_hba.conf that controls IP-based authentication configurations.
options.d: A planner cost coefficient that determines the relative penalty of random disk page reads versus sequential.

postanswer: CREATE RULE notify_order_insert AS ON INSERT TO orders DO ALSO NOTIFY new_order;

title: OWNER TO

options.a: An ALTER clause reassigning ownership of a database object and its administrative rights to a designated role.
options.b: A grant directive that permits non-owner roles to execute DDL modifications on a table without ownership rights.
options.c: A connection parameter specifying the target database user identity for connection authentication protocols.
options.d: A catalog attribute designating which operating system user originally initialized the PostgreSQL cluster dir.

postanswer: ALTER TABLE financial_records OWNER TO finance_admin;

title: RENAME TO

options.a: An ALTER clause that changes the identifier name of an existing database object in catalog schema tables.
options.b: A table migration utility that moves all relation heap files between different filesystem disk directories.
options.c: A query alias directive that renames projected columns in the client-facing output result set temporarily.
options.d: A connection routing rule that maps incoming client database requests to alternative database names online.

postanswer: ALTER TABLE legacy_users RENAME TO archived_users;

title: AND

options.a: Logical operator returning TRUE only if both boolean operands evaluate to TRUE, short-circuiting on FALSE.
options.b: Bitwise operator that computes the binary AND of two integer operands across all bit positions in memory.
options.c: Set operator that performs an intersection between two relational row streams from separate SELECT blocks.
options.d: A conditional operator that converts two expressions into an array pair for parallel element evaluation.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 50.00 AND in_stock = TRUE;

title: OR

options.a: A conditional fallback operator that returns the second expression only when the first expression evaluates to NULL.
options.b: Logical operator returning TRUE if either boolean operand evaluates to TRUE, short-circuiting if first is TRUE.
options.c: A pattern-matching delimiter used in regular expression searches inside LIKE clauses to separate word options.
options.d: Bitwise operator that computes the exclusive disjunction of binary byte values across integer column data types.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM tickets WHERE status = 'urgent' OR priority = 'high';

title: NOT

options.a: A constraint modifier that forces column values to reject empty string representations during insert queries.
options.b: An index optimization hint instructing the planner to ignore index scans on specified query filter columns.
options.c: Unary boolean operator inverting truth value: FALSE for TRUE, TRUE for FALSE, and preserving NULL as NULL.
options.d: A transaction directive that aborts the current statement if a null pointer or unassigned variable is found.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE NOT is_completed;

title: IN

options.a: A parameter mode indicator defining procedure arguments as strictly input-only read variables in function code.
options.b: A range restriction operator requiring values to fall strictly between two numeric boundary parameters in checks.
options.c: A pattern-matching predicate that checks whether a substring exists anywhere within a text string column.
options.d: Membership test evaluating if an expression matches any value in a literal list or subquery (= ANY equivalent).

options.c: Reverts a server configuration parameter that was prepared using ALTER SYSTEM in postgresql.auto.conf.
options.d: Aborts and rolls back a transaction previously prepared via 2-phase commit, releasing all held locks.

postanswer: ROLLBACK PREPARED 'tx_transfer_funds_1001';

title: SET TRANSACTION

options.a: Configures transaction characteristics (isolation level, read-write mode, deferrability) for transaction.
options.b: Assigns a custom numeric transaction ID to an unlogged batch processing operation on high-speed tables.
options.c: Overrides the server global default transaction isolation level permanently in postgresql.conf settings.
options.d: Binds a transaction to a specific CPU socket or NUMA node for optimized memory locality in hardware nodes.

postanswer: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE, READ ONLY;

title: ISOLATION LEVEL

options.a: A network security parameter defining TLS encryption strength for database connections from client apps.
options.b: Clause in SET TRANSACTION specifying concurrency degree (Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable).
options.c: A sandbox setting restricting untrusted procedural functions from accessing filesystem APIs on host OS.
options.d: A metric measuring the physical disk fragmentation between distinct database relations in storage pools.

postanswer: BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;

title: SERIALIZABLE

options.a: A data encoding format converting complex composite types into binary JSON streams for network transport.
options.b: An execution mode that forces query plans to execute strictly on a single CPU core without parallelism.
options.c: Highest SQL isolation level emulating strictly serial execution, using SIREAD locks to prevent anomalies.
options.d: A table storage option that stores rows sequentially in primary key order on physical disk heap blocks.

postanswer: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;

title: REPEATABLE READ

options.a: A lock escalation level converting row-level shared locks into exclusive table locks upon read collisions.
options.b: An isolation level allowing dirty reads of uncommitted tuples from concurrent active transactions in pool.
options.c: A transaction mode permitting read operations only while raising an immediate error on any write command.
options.d: Isolation level seeing a snapshot from the transaction first query, preventing non-repeatable reads in SQL.

postanswer: BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;

title: READ COMMITTED

options.a: Default PostgreSQL isolation level where each statement sees a new snapshot of committed data at start.
options.b: An isolation level that guarantees serializable execution ordering without tracking read-write conflicts.
options.c: A read-only transaction state that blocks write-ahead logging while allowing reads from shared buffers.
options.d: A transaction profile caching all read tuples in client memory to avoid repeated queries across sockets.

postanswer: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;

title: READ UNCOMMITTED

options.a: A high-performance isolation level that permits dirty reads of uncommitted rows from active transactions.
options.b: SQL-standard level conceptually allowing dirty reads, but implemented as READ COMMITTED in PostgreSQL.
options.c: A diagnostic mode inspecting corrupted shared buffer pages before crash recovery finishes on engine boot.
options.d: A maintenance state allowing administrative reads while a table is locked for exclusive rebuilding tasks.

postanswer: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ UNCOMMITTED;

title: GRANT

options.a: Bestows database object privileges (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE) or role membership to designated target roles.
options.b: An authentication directive generating temporary TLS certificates for external client network connections.
options.c: A configuration command that permanently sets role-level memory allowances in postgresql.conf on reload.
options.d: A transaction command elevating transaction isolation to Serializable for all subsequent query statements.

postanswer: GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON TABLE orders TO sales_role;

title: REVOKE

options.a: Permanently terminates active client connections associated with a specific user identity in cluster.
options.b: Removes previously granted database object privileges or role memberships from specified target roles.
options.c: Rolls back an uncommitted transaction and deletes its corresponding WAL segment from disk storage files.
options.d: Drops all database objects created by a specified user from system catalogs across all active schemas.

postanswer: REVOKE UPDATE ON TABLE employees FROM public;

title: ALL PRIVILEGES

options.a: Grants complete operating system root permissions to the PostgreSQL database daemon on the host machine.
options.b: An administration command that bypasses all security checks and row-level security policies on tables.
options.c: Shorthand specifier granting or revoking all applicable access permissions on a target database object.
options.d: A role attribute automatically assigning superuser status to a newly created database user in cluster.

postanswer: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE analytics_db TO data_admin;

title: WITH GRANT OPTION

options.a: A superuser permission allowing an administrator to create new physical database clusters on filesystem.
options.b: A clause in CREATE ROLE that authorizes the role to create additional database users in system catalogs.
options.c: An execution option permitting functions to execute with privileges of the defining role without checks.
options.d: Allows the recipient role to grant the conferred privileges on the target object to other database roles.

postanswer: GRANT SELECT ON accounts TO manager_role WITH GRANT OPTION;

title: ROW LEVEL SECURITY

options.a: Feature enforcing security policies controlling which rows are visible or modifiable for specific roles.
options.b: An encryption mechanism encrypting individual tuple attributes using distinct keys across relation heap.
options.c: A row-locking protocol preventing concurrent updates from modifying the same tuple during write tasks.
options.d: An access log audit system that records row-level read operations in server error logs for compliance.

postanswer: ALTER TABLE sensitive_user_data ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

title: BYPASSRLS

options.a: A query hint disabling index scans for queries running against row-level security tables during planning.
options.b: Role attribute permitting a role to bypass all Row-Level Security policies on all tables across database.
options.c: A connection parameter disabling client-side certificate validation during SSL cryptographic handshakes.
options.d: A table modifier that temporarily disables foreign key checking during bulk data loading operations on disk.

postanswer: ALTER ROLE backup_admin BYPASSRLS;

title: EXPLAIN

options.a: A documentation generator compiling comment metadata from system catalog tables into HTML documentation.
options.b: A server logging utility printing verbose SQL parse trees to PostgreSQL server logs during compilation.
options.c: Displays the execution plan generated by query planner, detailing plan nodes, costs, and row estimates.
options.d: A performance analysis tool profiling CPU register usage during query execution across background workers.

postanswer: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;

title: ANALYZE

options.a: Scans physical heap and index files for block checksum mismatches and filesystem disk corruption errors.
options.b: Recomputes index tree heights and merges underfull B-tree pages into adjacent leaf nodes on filesystem.
options.c: Monitors query response times in shared memory and logs slow queries exceeding log_min_duration_statement.
options.d: Collects statistics on column value distributions, storing them in pg_statistic for the query planner.

postanswer: ANALYZE VERBOSE customers;

title: VACUUM

options.a: Reclaims storage from dead tuples, updates FSM and VM maps, and freezes old transaction IDs against wrap.
options.b: Deallocates physical disk space from the operating system immediately by shrinking relation files to zero.
options.c: Clears all cached query execution plans and prepared statements from shared server memory on connection.
options.d: Removes temporary relations created by disconnected client sessions from temporary tablespace on disk.

postanswer: VACUUM (VERBOSE, ANALYZE) orders;

title: FULL

options.a: An index scan option that reads every index leaf page from start to finish without index probing on disk.
options.b: VACUUM modifier rewriting tables to new disk files to reclaim max space to OS, needing AccessExclusiveLock.
options.c: A buffer cache parameter forcing shared_buffers to retain cached pages without eviction during executions.
options.d: A replication mode ensuring transactions are written to all standby replicas before returning success.

postanswer: VACUUM FULL bloat_heavy_table;

title: FREEZE

options.a: Suspends all incoming client queries to create a consistent point-in-time filesystem snapshot on host.
options.b: Locks a relation in read-only mode, preventing subsequent INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE commands from clients.
options.c: VACUUM option aggressively freezing transaction IDs in tuple headers to advance wraparound thresholds.
options.d: Pauses background autovacuum worker processes during peak transaction processing hours in configuration.

postanswer: VACUUM FREEZE archived_transactions;

title: CLUSTER

options.a: Initializes a multi-node distributed database cluster across independent hardware servers in network.
options.b: Groups multiple related database tables into a shared storage volume for parallel I/O in file systems.
options.c: A replication command synchronizing schema objects across primary and secondary nodes during failover.
options.d: Physically reorders table heap storage to match the order of a B-tree index under an AccessExclusiveLock.

postanswer: CLUSTER orders USING idx_orders_customer_id;

title: REINDEX

options.a: Rebuilds an index using existing table data, recovering corrupted index pages and eliminating bloat cleanly.
options.b: Analyzes index selectivity and updates planner cost statistics in pg_statistic for optimizer algorithms.
options.c: Converts an existing B-tree index into a BRIN index to conserve disk storage on large append-only tables.
options.d: Re-reads index metadata from system catalogs into backend local memory cache during session initialize.

postanswer: REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY payment_history;

title: SHOW

options.a: Prints table data in a formatted terminal grid within interactive psql sessions for command exploration.
options.b: Displays current runtime value of a configuration parameter (GUC variable) in the active client session.
options.c: Lists all active client connections currently registered in pg_stat_activity on the host database node.
options.d: Outputs raw SQL definitions of a view or stored function from system catalogs to standard client stream.

postanswer: SHOW work_mem;

title: SET

options.a: A command permanently altering server configuration files on disk and triggering an engine reload event.
options.b: An internal compiler command instantiating user-defined types in catalog memory during server boot steps.
options.c: Modifies value of a runtime configuration parameter (GUC variable) for the current session or transaction.
options.d: Declares an enumerated set of allowed values for an application-specific domain type in schema DDL scripts.

postanswer: SET statement_timeout = '5s';

title: RESET

options.a: Flushes the shared buffer pool cache and clears prepared execution plans across all connected backends.
options.b: Re-reads postgresql.conf from disk and reloads configuration parameters without restarting the database.
options.c: Aborts all active transactions and resets transaction sequence counters back to zero during recovery.
options.d: Resets a runtime configuration parameter (or RESET ALL) back to its compiled or postgresql.conf default.

postanswer: RESET statement_timeout;

title: LISTEN

options.a: Registers current client backend session as a listener on a specific asynchronous notification channel.
options.b: Configures postmaster daemon to listen for incoming socket connections on a specified TCP network port.
options.c: Enables network traffic sniffing to capture raw PostgreSQL wire protocol packets for network debugging.
options.d: Starts an event monitor tracking filesystem I/O operations on the data directory for storage metrics.

postanswer: LISTEN order_events;

title: NOTIFY

options.a: Sends an automated email notification to the administrator when tablespace disk thresholds are exceeded.
options.b: Dispatches asynchronous notification events and payloads to listening client sessions on transaction commit.
options.c: Writes a persistent high-priority notification message directly into the PostgreSQL server activity log.
options.d: Broadcasts an internal cluster coordination message to standby replica instances to verify replication.

postanswer: NOTIFY order_events, 'order_123_paid';

title: UNLISTEN

options.a: Disables incoming TCP/IP connection listening on specific network interfaces in postgresql.conf settings.
options.b: Closes an active cursor portal and frees associated memory resources to prevent server session leaks.
options.c: Unregisters client session from listening to a specified notification channel (or all via UNLISTEN *).
options.d: Suppresses client-side notice and warning messages for the remainder of the session in wire protocol.

postanswer: UNLISTEN order_events;

title: LOAD

options.a: Streams bulk tabular data from an external CSV file directly into a heap relation on disk storage.
options.b: Restores a database cluster from a compressed pg_dump archive file using parallel restore worker threads.
options.c: Pre-warms the shared buffer pool by reading relation pages into RAM during server boot initialization.
options.d: Loads a dynamic shared library (.so file) into the PostgreSQL backend server process memory address space.

postanswer: LOAD '$libdir/plugins/my_custom_plugin';

title: DO

options.a: Executes anonymous inline procedural code blocks (PL/pgSQL, Python) without creating a stored function.
options.b: A loop control keyword iterating across result rows within a cursor portal in procedural SQL functions.
options.c: An execution clause forcing a query plan to execute immediately without cost-based planner optimization.
options.d: A transaction directive committing current statements in autonomous transactions without outer impacts.

postanswer: DO $$ BEGIN RAISE NOTICE 'Current database time: %', NOW(); END; $$;

title: CALL

options.a: Invokes a scalar function inside a SELECT statement expression list without transaction control options.
options.b: Invokes a stored PROCEDURE, supporting INOUT arguments and allowing transactional control in its body.
options.c: Dispatches an asynchronous remote procedure call to an external foreign server using foreign data wrappers.
options.d: Initiates a client-side macro command in interactive psql sessions for automated script execution flows.

postanswer: CALL recalculate_account_balances(2026, 'USD');

title: AS

options.a: A type-casting operator that forces implicit binary conversion between incompatible catalog data types.
options.b: An access method keyword specifying the physical storage format of partition leaf tables on disk drives.
options.c: Assigns an alias to a column, table, or CTE, or specifies the body definition of a function or procedure.
options.d: A security qualifier declaring a function to execute with caller permissions rather than definer rights.

postanswer: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders, AVG(amount) AS average_spend FROM orders;

title: CAST

options.a: A networking primitive that broadcasts replication messages across a local subnet to discover standbys.
options.b: A query rewrite rule transforming aggregation queries into window function trees before cost estimation.
options.c: A memory allocation directive that pins buffer pool pages in shared RAM to prevent eviction by LRU clock.
options.d: SQL syntax (CAST(expr AS type)) explicitly converting an expression between types, equivalent to :: syntax.

postanswer: SELECT CAST('2026-09-04' AS DATE), CAST(123.45 AS INTEGER);

title: LATERAL

options.a: Join modifier allowing a subquery or table function in FROM to reference columns from preceding FROM items.
options.b: A join method that evaluates relations in parallel across multiple worker nodes in query executor plans.
options.c: A horizontal table partitioning method distributing rows across physical disks using hash modulus keys.
options.d: An index scan option that reads leaf pages horizontally across the B-tree level without root traversal.

postanswer: SELECT d.dept_name, top_emp.name FROM departments d, LATERAL (SELECT name FROM employees e WHERE e.dept_id = d.id ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1) top_emp;

title: ONLY

options.a: A constraint modifier restricting column values to a single unique constant value across relation rows.
options.b: Modifier indicating query or DDL applies strictly to specified table, without recursing into child tables.
options.c: A concurrency clause that grants exclusive read access to a single transaction during serializable runs.
options.d: An isolation setting that prevents dirty reads during concurrent batch jobs without acquiring shared locks.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM ONLY parent_table;

title: COLLATE

options.a: Merges multiple small data extents into a continuous sequential block on disk during background vacuum.
options.b: A compression algorithm applied to TOAST tables storing large text attributes in out-of-line storage forks.
options.c: Overrides collation (linguistic sorting and comparison rules) for an expression, column, or index key.
options.d: A full-text search dictionary that groups derived words into root lexemes during document parsing runs.

postanswer: SELECT name FROM contacts ORDER BY name COLLATE "fr_FR";

title: CURRENT_DATE

options.a: A function querying operating system clocks upon each row evaluation, changing values during query run.
options.b: A timezone converter shifting UTC timestamps into server local timezone during presentation to clients.
options.c: A calendar utility that formats date values according to ISO-8601 representation for client wire packets.
options.d: Standard function returning calendar date at transaction start, remaining constant throughout transaction.

postanswer: SELECT * FROM subscriptions WHERE expiration_date >= CURRENT_DATE;

title: CURRENT_TIME

options.a: Standard function returning current time of day with timezone (timetz) at transaction start, held constant.
options.b: A timer measuring query execution duration in milliseconds and logging slow queries to server activity.
options.c: A high-resolution wall-clock function re-reading system time on every invocation throughout a transaction.
options.d: A connection parameter defining timeout thresholds for idle client sessions before disconnect triggers.

postanswer: SELECT CURRENT_TIME;

title: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

options.a: A function that increments a millisecond counter on every evaluated tuple during sequential heap scans.
options.b: Returns current date and time with timezone at transaction start, identical to transaction_timestamp().
options.c: A replication timestamp tracking when a WAL segment was replayed on a standby node across the network.
options.d: The creation timestamp recorded in pg_class when a relation was originally created by the DDL executor.

postanswer: INSERT INTO audits (recorded_at) VALUES (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);

title: CURRENT_USER

options.a: The operating system user account that owns the PostgreSQL server daemon process on the host machine.
options.b: The user role name that originally authenticated the current client network session during handshake.
options.c: Returns role name of effective user identity executing current statement (changes during SET ROLE).
options.d: A system catalog table that stores active connection credentials and authentication methods for roles.

postanswer: SELECT CURRENT_USER;

title: SESSION_USER

options.a: A temporary guest identity assigned to unauthenticated pooler sessions during initial handshake stages.
options.b: The user account used by background worker processes for autovacuum tasks and automatic maintenance runs.
options.c: An application role specified in the client connection string application_name parameter on connection.
options.d: Returns role name of user who established client connection session, remaining fixed during SET ROLE.

postanswer: SELECT SESSION_USER;

title: SYSTEM_USER

options.a: Returns authenticated identity and method of client connection (e.g. peer:name or scram-sha-256:name).
options.b: The root superuser account created during the initial database cluster bootstrap initialization sequence.
options.c: A pseudo-role owning internal system catalogs and internal C functions across all databases in cluster.
options.d: The operating system user that initiated the postmaster background process when starting the service.

postanswer: SELECT SYSTEM_USER;
